subject: fix(interactive): let the permission engine actually judge a bridged Claude approval; wire rewind
instruction:
fix(interactive): let the permission engine actually judge a bridged Claude approval; wire rewind

The C2 bridge built its permission subject in a shape the C1 engine never
read (tool_name/input rather than tool/command/paths/mode), so every
external approval normalised to an unknown tool and always asked; and it
called suggest/2 where the engine exports suggest/1, so suggested_rule was
always absent. The subject is now the engine's own request — Claude's tool
vocabulary mapped to the engine's, paths resolved against the call's cwd,
domains from a fetch URL — and a real-engine test proves a session-scope
Bash(git *) rule answers a bridged `git status` without a human.

interactive.rewind {id, to_turn, what?} and interactive.rewind_points reach
the native session's checkpoints through the same registry compact uses,
refused by transport elsewhere.

Acceptance. These tests are restored into the worktree after the session ends and must pass:
  - the durable engine allows a bridged command a session-scope rule names
  - rewind is operate, rewind_points is read, and both are advertised
  - rewind on a non-native transport is refused by transport, as wire data
  - rewind refuses a target that is neither a turn id nor an ordinal

Rules. Files that already exist under `test/` must not be modified or deleted — the change is graded against tests restored from the history after the session ends. New test files of your own are allowed and are left in place. Work only inside this worktree.
